title: Watson Brothers band and first Negro band at parties
summary: She recalls the homemade-instrument Watson Brothers serenading and playing for dances, then the first Negro band at home parties around 1920 with Celestin in it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well, I'm 52 years old, born and I moved to New Orange when I was three. And the first time I remember anything about jazz was at Pastor Shand, this small Negro band called the Watson Brothers. Started off the homemade instruments and they finally, by going around and serenading people in the evening, and people would go out and either pay them because they liked it or pay them to get away. They managed to acquire enough money to buy a few little, I think they had a banjo and a guitar, and I don't remember exactly all the various things that they did have. And they used to play what was, I suppose, jazz. But we loved it and they used to play on the, for dances we used to have on our end of the pier band house. And that was when I was maybe 12 or 13, 14. And then the first Negro band that I saw at playing at New Orleans parties was, when I was around 15 or 16, several people had, uh, dances at home. And they'd have, uh, this Negro band, Celestan, played in that band. And I don't remember whether it was his band or whether it was, he was just a member of it. Was that by 1920? That was around 1920, yeah. And, um, then I didn't see any more, hear any more jazz until we collect records. We had a lot of, you know, those, uh, what was it, Bessie Smith? The blues thing?
